page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfg6.6xlarge is an x86_64 architecture server instance powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 8269CY processor. Running on the KVM hypervisor, this instance provides 24 physical cores with a 1.0 thread-per-core configuration, operating at a clock speed of 3.1 GHz. The CPU features a 35 MB L3 cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 32 KB L1d cache, with support for AVX-512 vector extensions and AES cryptography. It is equipped with 96.0 GB of system memory, yielding a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core, and features a baseline network bandwidth of 8 Gbps. Local storage is not bundled with this instance.

In benchmark evaluations, the ecs.hfg6.6xlarge demonstrates stable mid-range performance. The processor achieves a single-core stress-ng score of 1438.39 and a multi-core score of 23015.19, complemented by a PassMark CPU score of 23637.6. Memory performance tests show a read-only small block cached bandwidth of 1282.13 GB/sec, which drops to 109.43 GB/sec for large block uncached reads, and 48.03 GB/sec for large block writes. For specialized workloads, the instance registers a Redis SET throughput of 22.14 million operations per second and a static web serving throughput of 17.13 GB/sec. Large language model inference speeds reach 1294.61 tokens per second for prompt processing on a small 135M model, and 34.44 tokens per second on a medium 7B model.

From a resource density perspective, the dedicated core allocation and 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio offer a balanced hardware profile for workloads requiring predictable CPU performance without the overhead of hyperthreading. The lack of local storage requires external block storage attachment, which represents a structural tradeoff for disk-heavy applications. This instance is suited for general-purpose workloads, multi-threaded decompression tasks, software compilation, database operations, and moderate web serving applications.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfg6.6xlarge is a general-purpose, x86_64 architecture server instance powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 8269CY processor. Operating at 3.1 GHz on the KVM hypervisor, it features 24 physical cores with single-thread execution, 96.0 GB of RAM, and a baseline network bandwidth of 8 Gbps, with no local storage included. Performance benchmarks indicate a balanced profile, with a PassMark CPU score of 23637.6, a Redis SET throughput of 22.14 million operations per second, and a static web serving throughput of 17.13 GB/sec. The instance also handles small-scale LLM inference, processing 1294.61 tokens per second for a 135M model. Lacking local storage, it relies on external volumes, making it a solid, predictable option for software compilation, database operations, multi-threaded decompression, and general-purpose enterprise applications.
